data.name: Carissima
data.gender_notes: Carissima is used as a unisex name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: From the Latin carissimus, meaning dearest or most dear. The name Carissima carries the meaning “Dear one” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Hebrew, Greek. Parents who choose Carissima usually hope their child will grow to embody dear one and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.etymology: Carissima belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “Dear one.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Carissima total 2, giving a life-path number of 2. Number 2 is linked with Moon and with the qualities of harmony, sensitivity and partnership.

in_hebrew.name: קאריסימה
in_hebrew.meaning: יקרissima היא שם נוצרי שמשמעותו 'יקרה ביותר' או 'אהובה מאוד'
in_hebrew.long_meaning: השם קאריסימה הוא שם נוצרי שמקורו בלטינית ומשמעותו 'יקרה ביותר' או 'אהובה מאוד'. הוא נגזר מהמילה הלטינית 'carus', שפירושה 'יקיר' או 'אהוב'. השם קאריסימה משמש לעתים קרובות ככינוי לנשים נוצריות שיקרות לאלוהים או לקהילתן.

in_greek.name: Καρισίμα
in_greek.long_meaning: Το όνομα Καρισίμα είναι ένα χριστιανικό όνομα που προέρχεται από το λατινικό όνομα Carissima, που σημαίνει 'πολύτιμη' ή 'αγαπημένη'. Στην Καινή Διαθήκη, η λέξη 'αγάπη' και οι παράγωγοί της είναι σημαντικοί όροι που εκφράζουν τη σχέση μεταξύ του Θεού και των πιστών.

data.spiritual_significance: The name "Carissima" carries a strong spiritual resonance, as it is derived from the Latin word for "dearest" or "most dear." In Christian theology, God is seen as the ultimate source of love and the giver of all good things. By using this name, we are reminded of the importance of keeping God as our dearest and most cherished companion, and of striving to emulate God's love and compassion in our own lives. Additionally, the name may be a reflection of the belief in the value and worth of all human beings as children of God, and the call to love and serve them as we would love and serve God himself.
